history.title: US Army targets 2028 for first high-energy laser counter-drone weapons
history.originalTitle: US Army targets 2028 for first high-energy laser counter-drone weapons

evidenceRecords.text: The first directed energy weapon selected by the U.S. Army for the Enduring-High Energy Laser (E-HEL) program could be out of testing and ready for counter-drone operations by early 2028, Army officials told Military Times at the Association of the U.S. Army’s annual meeting in Washington.

However, what we’ve seen is, with the environment as it is, everything that we produce as a capable counter-UAS system tends to get deployed somewhere,” said Kirk Williams, chief engineer at the U.S. Army Directed Energy Project Office.
In September, the Army awarded AeroVironment a $464.8 million contract for LOCUST X3, its modular, palletized high-energy laser system.
Earlier generations of the LOCUST system are actively fielded in operational environments, including at the U.S. southern border, according to AeroVironment.
The first LOCUST X3 is slated for delivery by Q4 of FY 2027 and will be mounted on the Joint Light Tactical Vehicle.
That would be a great win for the Army.” It is unclear where the first high-energy counter-drone weapons under H-ELS will be deployed.

The counter-drone E-HEL contract is for more than 26 laser weapons units total, according to AeroVironment vice president of Directed Energy, John Garrity, who indicated the initial system is on target for 2027 delivery.
“We would love to be able to keep the first unit off the line for our testing and training.
The goal is to push it through testing, validation, verification and “give it to soldiers as soon as possible,” said Brig.
Gen. Guy Yelverton, capability program executive for Defensive Fires. “My far-down point would be spring [2028], and if I could get in the December-January timeframe, that would be awesome.
That would be a great win for the Army.”
It is unclear where the first high-energy counter-drone weapons under H-ELS will be deployed.
Yelverton suggested the 7th Infantry Division could be a potential partner.

Deputy commanding officer of Support for the 7th Infantry Division, Col. Charles Kean, described directed-energy weapons as a component of defense against high-echelon air threats, including individual UAS or formations, but said they were not a “single bullet” solution.

history.title: Army Wants High-Energy Laser Weapons It Can Put On “Any Vehicle In The Motorpool”
history.originalTitle: Army Wants High-Energy Laser Weapons It Can Put On “Any Vehicle In The Motorpool”

evidenceRecords.text: The U.S. Army is pursuing a family of modular and scalable laser directed energy weapons that can be fitted to any vehicle in its inventory.

The Army is already fielding high-energy lasers operationally on a limited basis, including along the border wth Mexico , but the technology has faced continued hurdles to more widespread use in recent years.

Army officials and industry representatives discussed what is currently called the Enduring-High Energy Laser (E-HEL) program during a panel discussion this week at the Association of the U.S. Army’s (AUSA) main annual convention , at which TWZ was in attendance.
In September, AeroVironment received the first production contract under E-HEL to supply examples of its 30-kilowatt-class LOCUST X3 laser directed energy weapon system.

The Army has already acquired earlier LOCUST variants, including vehicle-mounted and palletized types , through more experimental programs, and these are the systems now deployed along the southern border.
“We’re focused on any vehicle in the motorpool.
I want to try to integrate future capability of high-energy lasers into it,” Army Brig.

“I can now look at any formation type to be able to put a high-energy laser capability into it for the counter-UAS [uncrewed aerial systems] fight.” “That gives me even more opportunities to share this capability across all Army formations, and give our senior leaders [the] maximum amount of thought process and input into where the system goes, who the soldier is that’s operating it, and I’ve given them quite a solution,” he added.
The gaming accessory is part of KBR’s Firefly, a mobile high-energy laser weapon system developed by Kord Technologies.
Recently, the Pentagon selected the company for a pilot program to test defending U.S. military installations against adversarial drones.
The system uses a concentrated beam of light instead of costly missile interceptors, potentially offering a less expensive way to bring down drones.
The pilot program will place directed-energy weapons at military bases across the country for a yearlong assessment, where service members will operate, maintain and collect data on the weapons.
The Pentagon will, in turn, gather information on cost and logistics.
KBR subsidiary Kord has marketed Firefly as a palletized mobile laser.
The company said the system — part of which looks like a futuristic, modular cell phone camera lens — can operate in temperatures ranging from negative 15 to 35 degrees Celsius.
During an August demonstration in Alabama, company officials said that a truck-mounted system needs just a few seconds to down a small drone.

events.title: Simulation App Speeds Up Electric Truck Battery Design
events.originalTitle: Simulation App Speeds Up Electric Truck Battery Design
events.excerpt: To help overcome the issue of battery lifetime, a consortium of universities and industry partners incorporated multiscale simulation and a custom simulation app into the battery manufacturing process. The organizations involved in this project were Aurobay, Resolvent, the European Commission, the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), Vinnova (the Swedish Agency for Innovation Systems), Innovation Fund Denmark, and Volvo Group Trucks Operations.

evidenceRecords.text: To help overcome the issue of battery lifetime, a consortium of universities and industry partners incorporated multiscale simulation and a custom simulation app into the battery manufacturing process.

The organizations involved in this project were Aurobay, Resolvent, the European Commission, the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), Vinnova (the Swedish Agency for Innovation Systems), Innovation Fund Denmark, and Volvo Group Trucks Operations.
The simulation app, built by Resolvent, a Denmark-based engineering consultancy that specializes in green energy, enables the R&D department at Volvo to easily test battery lifetime performance.
The Multiscale Simulation of Laser Welding for Optimal Battery Pack Manufacturing project — referred to as “LaserBATMAN” — was initiated in May 2022 and wrapped up in May 2025 (Ref.
Although BATMAN here refers to battery manufacturing and not the famous masked superhero, the goals for the project also strove for greatness.
The LaserBATMAN project aimed to optimize two key performance metrics for battery packs: robustness and lifetime (Ref.

One element of the battery manufacturing process that affects both of these metrics is the laser welding used in component joining processes (for example, to connect battery cells in a pack via a busbar).
Computational modeling can be used to analyze and predict the effects of welding and joining processes at different stages of the manufacturing process.

“Ambitions grew,” Nielsen said, explaining that the team ended up modeling the performance of the entire battery, from cell to pack level, and even “turned [the model] into a design tool in the end”, in reference to the app.
After training the deep neural network of the battery model, the team built a custom simulation app to efficiently optimize busbar tabs in the configuration of a battery pack.
After training the DNN of the battery model, the team built a custom simulation app to efficiently optimize busbar tabs in the configuration of a battery pack.

COMSOL A “Tool Within a Tool” for Busbar Weld Design The different features of the simulation app, as described by Nielsen, include its options to input dimensions for the pack geometry (Figure 3), the number of cells, and operating conditions such as ambient temperature and charge–discharge current profiles.

topicPlan.title: 无人僚机竞速：从单机首飞到空战编组
topicPlan.angle: 回答协同作战飞机如何从厂商自主试飞走向有人机在空指挥的实战化验证，以及这一转变对空军采购节奏意味着什么。以YFQ-48A首次全自主飞行（含滑行、起降）与F-22飞行员在座舱内指挥YFQ-44A半自主执行战术指令两条进展为证据，说明CCA已跨越'能飞'与'能协同'两段距离；同时指出Increment 2需求未定、多家厂商并跑带来的时间与预算约束，以及当前演示均为单独无人机、未涉及多机编组或对抗环境，尚不能证明作战效能。

topicPlan.title: 激光反无人机：基地防御先落地，机动化仍是问号
topicPlan.angle: 回答定向能反无人机为何先在固定基地和边境试点落地、而不是直接上车伴随部队。以KBR的Firefly移动激光入选五角大楼本土基地反无人机试点、陆军E-HEL项目2028年前形成初始作战能力并已向AeroVironment订购LOCUST X3为证据，梳理'模块化、可上任何车辆'的愿景与功率、供电、后勤现实之间的落差；并借助韩国Hanwha在军演中用固定与车载激光击落三架靶机作为横向参照，说明这类系统在多国仍处于演示与有限部署阶段，实战拦截高速或饱和集群能力尚不清楚。

history.title: Northrop Grumman’s Talon Blue Collaborative Combat Aircraft Has Flown
history.originalTitle: Northrop Grumman’s Talon Blue Collaborative Combat Aircraft Has Flown

evidenceRecords.text: We have a significant update on the fast-moving world of Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) out of Mojave, California today.
Northrop Grumman’s Talon Blue, which now has the official designation YFQ-48A, has taken to the skies for the first time.

Talon Blue flying out of Mojave Air and Space Port for the first time. (@Task_Force23) TASK_FORCE23 The uncrewed aircraft took to the skies over Mojave Air and Space Port, home of famed ‘bleeding0edge’ airframer and Northrop Grumman subsidiary Scaled Composites, which built the aircraft.

A release from Northrop Grumman reads: “MOJAVE, Calif. – Oct. 3, 2026 – Northrop Grumman’s (NYSE: NOC) YFQ-48A Talon Blue completed its first fully autonomous flight, including taxi, takeoff, in-flight maneuvers, and landing.
The flight builds on Northrop Grumman’s seven decades of autonomy experience and more than 500,000 autonomous flight hours, with lessons from Talon Blue informing future autonomous systems.

Details on YFQ-48A Talon Blue: Talon Blue is part of Northrop Grumman’s internally-funded Project Talon portfolio focused on accelerating the development of mission-ready autonomous airpower capabilities.

Every flight and lesson strengthens our broader autonomy work and sharpens what comes next.” Talon Blue flying above the Mojave Desert in California. (Northrop Grumman) While the Talon Blue aircraft draws most of the attention, Northrop Grumman has put great emphasis on its back-end autonomy development ecosystem, which includes its purpose-built Model 437 demonstrator aircraft , now under the Talon IQ badge (formerly Beacon).

Talon Blue is entering a growing field of CCA offerings, with extremely intense competition, that are primarily aimed at equipping the USAF with its next CCA acquisition of hundreds of aircraft known as Increment 2 , for which the requirements remain undefined.

Many more types are on the horizon, including those from new players and globally from foreign manufacturers . (@Task_Force23) TASK_FORCE23 (@Task_Force23) TASK_FORCE23 With the loss of the F/A-XX next-generation naval fighter program to Boeing, Northrop Grumman winning a contract from the U.S. services for Talon Blue has become more important.

history.title: Northrop Grumman’s YFQ-48A CCA completes first fully autonomous flight
history.originalTitle: Northrop Grumman’s YFQ-48A CCA completes first fully autonomous flight

evidenceRecords.text: Northrop Grumman’s YFQ-48A Talon Blue Collaborative Combat Aircraft recently completed its first fully autonomous flight.
Talon Blue executed its first fully autonomous flight in Mojave, California, which included taxi, takeoff, in-flight maneuvers and landing, according to a recent company release .
Talon Blue executed its first fully autonomous flight in Mojave, California, which included taxi, takeoff, in-flight maneuvers and landing, according to a recent company release.
“Our customers made it clear they need autonomous systems that can be fielded faster and more affordably without sacrificing mission effectiveness.
We listened,” Craig Woolston, vice president and general manager of research and advanced design at Northrop Grumman, said in the release.
A pilot flying an F-22 Raptor fighter has issued commands to a YFQ-44A Fury Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) drone in a first-of-its-kind test.
An Anduril spokesperson confirmed directly to TWZ that this was a first for an F-22 and a pre-production YFQ-44A.
“During the demonstration, an F-22 pilot served as an airborne ‘quarterback,’ issuing high-level tactical directives to a single YFQ-44A,” according to a press release from the Air Force .

“The aircraft’s onboard autonomy software interpreted and executed those directives in real time, conducting dynamic flight maneuvers and simulated combat tasks.” A stock picture of an F-22 Raptor test jet.

USAF “The event brought together personnel from the 412th Test Wing, 422nd Test and Evaluation Squadron, 309th Software Engineering Group, Experimental Operations Unit, F-22 System Program Office and the CCA Software Autonomy and Teaming Branch,” according to the Air Force release.
The Experimental Operations Unit (EOU) mentioned here is based at Nellis Air Force Base in Nevada and has been leading efforts to pave the way for future Air Force CCA operations.
The “Fury and an F-22 both took off [from] Edwards AFB [Air Force Base in California] and joined up midair,” according to a separate release from Anduril.

“While in flight, the Raptor pilot sent an updated mission plan to Fury using a tactical data link, commanding Fury through operationally-relevant maneuvers from the cockpit of the crewed quarterback.” Neither the Air Force nor Anduril provided further details on how the F-22 was configured for this test.

Cheongwang fired on a drone overhead that “caught fire and fell from the sky,” The Korea Times reported from the exercise at a training ground in Yangpyeong, Gyeonggi Province.
The laser was one part of a layered counter-drone demonstration that also included electronic jamming and a K21 armored vehicle firing on incoming drones.
Hanwha did not say which system destroyed which drones, what kinds of drones were used, what vehicle carries the newer laser or the range of either weapon.

The Oct. 14 demonstration followed a Sept. 16 event at South Korea’s 2026 Defense Drone Technology Exhibition, where Cheongwang downed four drones and two larger unmanned aircraft in succession, Hanwha said.
Cheongwang, meaning “light of the sky,” in Korean is formally known as the Laser Air Defense Weapon Block-I.
Hanwha developed it under a program led by South Korea’s Agency for Defense Development.
The company calls it the world’s first operationally deployed laser weapon.

South Korea first fielded the system in December 2024 and had about five units at major government facilities as of June, including the Ministry of National Defense building, according to Korea JoongAng Daily .
North Korean drones have repeatedly violated South Korean airspace.

evidenceRecords.text: To help overcome the issue of battery lifetime, a consortium of universities and industry partners incorporated multiscale simulation and a custom simulation app into the battery manufacturing process.

The organizations involved in this project were Aurobay, Resolvent, the European Commission, the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), Vinnova (the Swedish Agency for Innovation Systems), Innovation Fund Denmark, and Volvo Group Trucks Operations.
The simulation app, built by Resolvent, a Denmark-based engineering consultancy that specializes in green energy, enables the R&D department at Volvo to easily test battery lifetime performance.
The Multiscale Simulation of Laser Welding for Optimal Battery Pack Manufacturing project — referred to as “LaserBATMAN” — was initiated in May 2022 and wrapped up in May 2025 (Ref.
Although BATMAN here refers to battery manufacturing and not the famous masked superhero, the goals for the project also strove for greatness.
The LaserBATMAN project aimed to optimize two key performance metrics for battery packs: robustness and lifetime (Ref.

One element of the battery manufacturing process that affects both of these metrics is the laser welding used in component joining processes (for example, to connect battery cells in a pack via a busbar).
Computational modeling can be used to analyze and predict the effects of welding and joining processes at different stages of the manufacturing process.

“Ambitions grew,” Nielsen said, explaining that the team ended up modeling the performance of the entire battery, from cell to pack level, and even “turned [the model] into a design tool in the end”, in reference to the app.
After training the deep neural network of the battery model, the team built a custom simulation app to efficiently optimize busbar tabs in the configuration of a battery pack.

COMSOL A “Tool Within a Tool” for Busbar Weld Design The different features of the simulation app, as described by Nielsen, include its options to input dimensions for the pack geometry (Figure 3), the number of cells, and operating conditions such as ambient temperature and charge–discharge current profiles.

issues.detail: 联盟组成、Resolvent开发应用、项目2025年5月结项均有依据，且正确指出未给周期或成本降幅；但“项目已结项”与“瑞典与丹麦资助方”均属原文，注意“欧洲委员会”被写成“欧盟”资助方，尚可接受；不过“封装成研发可操作的定制应用”中“研发可操作”是推断，原文仅说易于测试寿命；整体接近合格但仍有轻微增译。
“只说明做了深度神经网络训练，未给出验证工况与误差范围”有依据；但“训练数据的覆盖范围”是推断性约束，原文未直接讨论训练数据覆盖范围，属于分析延伸，尚可接受；然而“加速承诺”在报道中并非明确承诺，而是应用目的，措辞略强。整体部分支持。
“与只针对单一焊接工序的建模相比”这一比较对象在证据中并未明确出现，原文只讲计算建模可分析焊接与连接过程；本项目扩展到整包和设计工具有依据，但“只针对单一焊接工序”是未证实的对照，构成比较性增译。
章节围绕“验证加速效果”的问题给出了判断，并解释了代理模型与定制应用的具体机制，也说明了边界与后续核对点，整体有分析深度；但b4s0中“与只针对单一焊接工序的建模相比”缺少证据支持的比较对象，属于未证实的对照，容易把推断当作已知差异。需修改comparison段第一句，去掉或软化“只针对单一焊接工序”这一未证实的比较项
